title: Rivers Inside the Sea
question: What drives ocean currents, and how do they shape climate?
hook: Northwest Europe owes its mild weather to water that set out from the equatorial Atlantic.
idea: Wind pushes surface currents and density differences drive deep ones, and together they carry heat around the globe, shaping the climate of whole regions.

beats.prompt: Match each kind of moving water to its description
pairs: Surface water pushed forward by the prevailing wind
More definite direction, faster than a drift
Larger masses of water, faster than either
beats.explain: Moving seawater is classed by velocity, size and direction, from slow wind-pushed drifts up to large, fast streams like the Gulf Stream.

beats.prompt: Put these steps of the Atlantic conveyor in order
items: Surface water travels polewards from the equatorial Atlantic
It sinks at high latitudes as North Atlantic Deep Water
The dense water flows on into the ocean basins
beats.explain: Wind-driven surface water heads polewards, cools en route, sinks at high latitudes, and then spreads as dense water into the ocean basins.

beats.prompt: Suppose the current bringing warm water up the north Atlantic to northwest Europe stopped. What would you expect along those coasts?

choices.label: Ice could form along shores and block ships
Coasts would warm as the heat stayed put
choices.feedback: The current is what delivers the heat; without it the coasts lose warmth rather than gain it.

choices.label: Nothing would change, since air alone sets climate
choices.feedback: Ocean currents strongly influence the temperature of the regions they pass through.

choices.label: Ports would dry out as the sea level fell
choices.feedback: The current's role here is heat, not the height of the sea.

beats.explain: That warm current slowly keeps ice from forming along the seashores, ice that would otherwise block ships from seaports and inland waterways.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Surface currents are generally driven by wind systems.
Deep-water currents are driven by differences in water density.
Seawater density depends on its temperature and salt content.
So deep currents can only start where the wind blows hardest.
beats.explain: Deep circulation is driven by density gradients created by surface heat and freshwater fluxes, not by where the wind is strongest.
